issue.title: Marked-Patch bulk launch (leader `,<space>`) launches one agent instead of N
issue.description:
ACE leader-mode `,<space>` on the Patches/Artifacts tab with marks calls `_start_agents_from_marked()` (src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_entry_bulk.py), which fills `self._bulk_patches` with every marked Patch, notifies 'Running agent on N marked Patch(s)', and shows ONE prompt bar. Nothing reads `_bulk_patches` any more: its only reader was `_launch_bulk.py`'s `BulkLaunchMixin`, which ran solely from the discarded `proc_callable` and was therefore already dead in production before it was deleted in 0f7d86a66 (phase sase-ng.1.4). The durable path submits a single RUN_LAUNCH for the shared prompt, so N marked Patches launch exactly one agent while the notification claims N.

REPRODUCTION: mark 2+ Patches in ACE, press leader `,<space>`, submit a prompt -> one agent appears, notification said N.

IMPACT: silent under-launch on a bound, user-facing action; the count in the toast is wrong.

SCOPE: give the durable launch path a per-Patch fan-out so each marked Patch gets its own `sase run` submission with that Patch's project/cl context, or (if fan-out is rejected) correct the notification and the leader-mode affordance to say one agent. `_bulk_patches` is still declared in _entry_bulk.py and _entry_points.py and is currently write-only. The deleted per-Patch dispatch logic is recoverable from 0f7d86a66^:src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_launch_bulk.py.

NOT caused by epic sase-ng.1 -- that epic removed the already-unreachable copy and recorded this gap deliberately (see its plan's 'Deliberately not restored here' section). The regression dates to 0835b38d2, which moved launch to durable argv submission. Originating bead sase-ng; proposed by phase sase-ng.1.6.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-p7 — the other capability epic sase-ng.1 deliberately left unrestored when it deleted the unreachable in-process launch body; both are recoverable from the same deletion commits and share the ACE launch-submit surface (_launch_start.py / _launch_resolved_prompt).
